name: Ruwa

queries.query: Ruwa Zimbabwe official cadastral parcel map GIS land registry cadastral map; Zimbabwe official cadastral map parcel GIS Surveyor General land registry Ruwa
queries.result: First-party discovery identified the Department of the Surveyor General as Zimbabwe's cadastral custodian and the Ruwa Local Board as the local authority. Official material describes cadastral records and an electronic cadastre, but no public Ruwa parcel viewer, current JavaScript/configuration, or anonymous parcel ID-plus-geometry endpoint was found.

queries.query: Ruwa Zimbabwe mepu yeminda cadastre GIS kunyoresa ivhu; Zimbabwe Surveyor General mepu yeminda yepamutemo
queries.result: The Shona-language discovery variant did not identify a first-party Shona parcel viewer or public parcel API. The same official Zimbabwe Surveyor General, Parliament, Ministry of Lands, and Ruwa Local Board sources were the relevant first-party leads; no local public geometry service was exposed.

registryEvidence.custodian: The Department of the Surveyor General is evidenced in official Zimbabwe material as the national cadastral survey and mapping custodian; Ruwa Local Board is evidenced as the local authority.
registryEvidence.scopeNote: National Surveyor General and Ministry material is not evidence of a Ruwa-local public parcel service. No local cadastral custodian endpoint, public viewer, or anonymous parcel feed was qualified.

parcelDiscovery.note: No safe anonymous parcel ID-plus-geometry response was obtained. The exact WUP point was preserved and was not shifted or used as a citywide absence test.

requestOutcomes.outcome: HTTP 200. Official local-board site loaded, but page inspection exposed no public cadastral viewer, map service configuration, parcel layer, schema, CRS, native parcel ID, or geometry endpoint.
HTTP 200. Official Ministry site loaded. Its client-charter material describes Surveyor General cadastral survey and mapping functions, not an anonymous public parcel API.

Official Parliament material states Zimbabwe's electronic cadastre was still incomplete/in development and identifies Surveyor General, Deeds, and councils as separate data stakeholders; it exposed no public parcel geometry service.
TLS certificate verification failed because the local issuer was unavailable; verification was preserved and no exception was used. No login or private land-record access was attempted.
HTTP 200 login page. Authentication-backed system; no login, credentials, tokens, owner, address, titleholder, or other unsafe fields were requested. No anonymous parcel geometry was exposed.
HTTP 200 official government portal. General portal content exposed no Ruwa cadastral map/API or safe parcel response.

safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel identifier only if publicly exposed and source-proven
uncertainty: National cadastral and land-information systems may expose authenticated or non-indexed data; no login or private access was attempted.
The Parliament evidence that the electronic cadastre was incomplete is project-status evidence, not proof of citywide parcel absence.
The TLS failure is transport evidence only and is not evidence of cadastral absence.
No parcel polygon is retained because no safe source geometry and stable native identity were verified.
Independent serial review is required before any adapter or runtime qualification.
